title: Computer, Automated Teller, and Office Machine Repairers
description: Repair, maintain, or install computers, word processing systems, automated teller machines, and electronic office machines, such as duplicating and fax machines.

tasks.text: Reassemble machines after making repairs or replacing parts.
Converse with customers to determine details of equipment problems.
Disassemble machines to examine parts, such as wires, gears, or bearings for wear or defects, using hand or power tools and measuring devices.
Advise customers concerning equipment operation, maintenance, or programming.
Align, adjust, or calibrate equipment according to specifications.
Repair, adjust, or replace electrical or mechanical components or parts, using hand tools, power tools, or soldering or welding equipment.
Travel to customers' stores or offices to service machines or to provide emergency repair service.
Maintain parts inventories and order any additional parts needed for repairs.
Operate machines to test functioning of parts or mechanisms.
Reinstall software programs or adjust settings on existing software to fix machine malfunctions.
Clean, oil, or adjust mechanical parts to maintain machines' operating efficiency and to prevent breakdowns.
Maintain records of equipment maintenance work or repairs.
Test new systems to ensure that they are in working order.
Complete repair bills, shop records, time cards, or expense reports.
Install and configure new equipment, including operating software or peripheral equipment.
Analyze equipment performance records to assess equipment functioning.
Read specifications, such as blueprints, charts, or schematics, to determine machine settings or adjustments.
Update existing equipment, performing tasks such as installing updated circuit boards or additional memory.
Test components or circuits of faulty equipment to locate defects, using oscilloscopes, signal generators, ammeters, voltmeters, or special diagnostic software programs.
Assemble machines according to specifications, using hand or power tools and measuring devices.
Lay cable and hook up electrical connections between machines, power sources, and phone lines.
Enter information into computers to copy programs from one electronic component to another or to draw, modify, or store schematics.
Fill machines with toners, inks, or other duplicating fluids.
Train new repairers.
Calibrate testing instruments.

skills.name: Active Listening
skills.def: Giving full attention to what other people are saying, taking time to understand the points being made, asking questions as appropriate, and not interrupting at inappropriate times.

skills.name: Repairing
skills.def: Repairing machines or systems using the needed tools.

skills.name: Critical Thinking
skills.def: Using logic and reasoning to identify the strengths and weaknesses of alternative solutions, conclusions, or approaches to problems.

skills.name: Complex Problem Solving
skills.def: Identifying complex problems and reviewing related information to develop and evaluate options and implement solutions.

skills.name: Troubleshooting
skills.def: Determining causes of operating errors and deciding what to do about it.

skills.name: Speaking
skills.def: Talking to others to convey information effectively.

skills.name: Equipment Selection
skills.def: Determining the kind of tools and equipment needed to do a job.

skills.name: Equipment Maintenance
skills.def: Performing routine maintenance on equipment and determining when and what kind of maintenance is needed.

skills.name: Quality Control Analysis
skills.def: Conducting tests and inspections of products, services, or processes to evaluate quality or performance.

skills.name: Time Management
skills.def: Managing one's own time and the time of others.

skills.name: Reading Comprehension
skills.def: Understanding written sentences and paragraphs in work-related documents.

skills.name: Operations Monitoring
skills.def: Watching gauges, dials, or other indicators to make sure a machine is working properly.

skills.name: Writing
skills.def: Communicating effectively in writing as appropriate for the needs of the audience.

skills.name: Active Learning
skills.def: Understanding the implications of new information for both current and future problem-solving and decision-making.

skills.name: Monitoring
skills.def: Monitoring/Assessing performance of yourself, other individuals, or organizations to make improvements or take corrective action.

skills.name: Coordination
skills.def: Adjusting actions in relation to others' actions.

skills.name: Service Orientation
skills.def: Actively looking for ways to help people.

skills.name: Installation
skills.def: Installing equipment, machines, wiring, or programs to meet specifications.

skills.name: Judgment and Decision Making
skills.def: Considering the relative costs and benefits of potential actions to choose the most appropriate one.

skills.name: Social Perceptiveness
skills.def: Being aware of others' reactions and understanding why they react as they do.

skills.name: Spreadsheet software
skills.def: Software to create or edit numbers or text organized into rows and columns of cells. May include formulas which recalculate values based on other cells. Examples: Microsoft Excel.

skills.name: Office suite software
skills.def: Software to provide word processing, spreadsheet, e-mail, presentations, or data management capabilities. Examples: Microsoft Office software.

skills.name: Data base user interface and query software
skills.def: Software to query, present, or edit information stored in a database sytem. Examples: Database software, Microsoft Access, ServiceNow, Structured query language SQL.

skills.name: Web platform development software
skills.def: Software to create or maintain applications accessed through web sites or using web technologies such as HTML. Examples: Hypertext markup language HTML, JavaScript, Microsoft Active Server Pages ASP.

skills.name: Operating system software
skills.def: Software to provide the operational interface to a computer and provide higher-level services and APIs. Examples: Linux, Microsoft Windows, UNIX.

skills.name: Electronic mail software
skills.def: Software to compose, send, or receive email. Examples: Email software, IBM Notes, Microsoft Exchange, Microsoft Outlook.
